title: The Tamsin Hale Casebook
tagline: One detective. One assistant. One small dog. A new case in a new corner of the world.

detective.name: Tamsin Hale
detective.look: late thirties, short dark curls, round tortoiseshell glasses, long olive travel coat with many pockets, leather satchel, magnifier on a cord
detective.method: notices what people carry, not what they say; keeps a pocket casebook with a pressed flower for every solved case

assistant.name: Barnaby Okafor
assistant.look: tall, bow tie, flat cap, rolled maps under one arm
assistant.skill: maps, languages, train timetables; always asks the question that unlocks the case

dog.name: Biscuit
dog.role: small wire-haired terrier, nose of the team
dog.look: cream and brown, one ear up, one ear down, red collar with a tiny brass bell
dog.skill: finds the thing that is out of place; comic relief; never in danger

bible.tone: cozy, witty, gentle: no murder, no gore, no on-page violence, no romance; crimes are thefts, forgeries, disappearances, impostors, sabotage, pranks gone wrong
recurring: each volume ends with Tamsin pressing a flower from the place into her casebook
a running letter from a mysterious patron, one fragment per volume, revealed in volume 12
rules: every volume has a new setting, a new cast of suspects and a new way of combining clues
inspired by a public-domain story or legend; credit line on cover and first page; all names, plots and puzzles are new
puzzle answers are built by code and verified by an independent solver; AI never decides an answer
each volume borrows ONE general trick of the genre (listed as `method`) and at most the idea of a public-domain story (US publication 1930 or earlier); plot, names, solution and puzzles are new

volumes.title: The Moonstone Affair
volumes.clue_mechanic: alibi timeline grid (who was where, hour by hour)

arc_clue.found: the stud is sewn into the lining of the stolen jewel's travelling case; engraved with a tiny mapmaker's mark Tamsin knows from home

volumes.method: the unknowing culprit (someone moved the jewel in their sleep, so every alibi is honest)

volumes.title: The Worn-Out Slippers of Halvern Hall
volumes.setting: a snowbound manor with a hidden ballroom
volumes.clue_mechanic: wear-pattern map overlay (trace the paths the slippers took)

twists.maze: drawn on a transparent-style overlay of the manor plan
twists.wordsearch: words run along the dance steps

arc_clue.found: a stud fixed under the heel of the twelfth slipper; Barnaby notices the same mark on a manor floor plan dated the year Odile vanished

volumes.method: the secret route (a hidden passage makes the impossible journey possible)

volumes.title: The Ghost Ship Ledger
volumes.setting: a drifting merchant brig and a harbour office, 1870s
volumes.clue_mechanic: two documents that contradict each other (spot the lie)

twists.cryptogram: ship's code flags instead of letters

arc_clue.found: the brig's ledger lists a passenger 'O. H., cartographer' who paid with a brass stud

volumes.method: the contradicting record (one of two official documents was quietly rewritten)

volumes.title: The Lamp-Lit Locked Room

inspired_by.work: The Murders in the Rue Morgue (locked-room idea only; no violence, a theft)
inspired_by.author: Edgar Allan Poe

volumes.clue_mechanic: floor-plan elimination (what could not have entered)

twists.logicgrid: rooms and doors instead of people

arc_clue.found: the locked room's music stand hides a stud; the conservatory's founder once ordered a map 'of a place that keeps moving'

volumes.method: the locked room with a non-human entrant (something small came through a gap no person could use)

volumes.title: The Clockwork Nightingale
volumes.setting: an emperor's winter conservatory of automata
volumes.clue_mechanic: rhythm and music-box cipher (read the pins on the cylinder)
volumes.final_form: a melody that spells the culprit's alias

twists.shift: a keyboard shift instead of the alphabet
twists.cbn: the picture is a music-box cylinder

arc_clue.found: the clockwork nightingale sings eight notes; the second stud of its kind sits in its key, and the notes match the compass bearings so far

volumes.method: the mechanical impostor (a machine performs while its owner is elsewhere)

volumes.title: The Woman in the Grey Shawl
volumes.setting: a seaside town and its portrait gallery
volumes.clue_mechanic: family tree and identity matching (who is who)

arc_clue.found: a portrait in the gallery shows a woman in a grey shawl holding Odile's unfinished atlas, a stud painted on its clasp

volumes.method: the swapped identity (two look-alike people trade places for one evening)

volumes.title: The Lost Colony Carving
volumes.setting: a misty island and its abandoned fort
volumes.clue_mechanic: directional chain (follow the carved arrows and place names)
volumes.final_form: map coordinates of the hiding place

twists.wordsearch: place names on a coastal map

arc_clue.found: a carving on the island fort repeats the mapmaker's mark and gives the first true bearing: the compass was never broken

volumes.method: the message left behind (a carved word that means something else to the right reader)

volumes.title: The Golden City Cipher
volumes.setting: a mountain archive and a hidden valley
volumes.clue_mechanic: stacked cipher layers (each layer opens the next)
volumes.final_form: layered decode that names the patron's courier

arc_clue.found: the patron's courier carries the eighth stud and a sealed note: 'four more, and you will find her'

volumes.method: the layered cipher (each solved layer is the key to the next)

volumes.title: The Bell That Rang Itself
volumes.setting: an alpine bell foundry and its clock tower, winter fair night

inspired_by.work: The Adventure of the Speckled Band (mechanism idea only)
inspired_by.author: Arthur Conan Doyle

volumes.clue_mechanic: sound-and-timing chart (who could hear which bell, when)
volumes.final_form: cord-and-pulley diagram of how it was done

arc_clue.found: the ninth stud is cast into the smallest bell; its maker's ledger shows Odile ordered it

volumes.method: the remote mechanism (the bell is rung from far away by a hidden cord)

volumes.title: The Postmark in Plain Sight
volumes.setting: a canal city's grand sorting office the week before New Year
volumes.clue_mechanic: hidden-in-plain-sight search (the obvious object is the disguise)

twists.wordsearch: words hidden in a page of postmarks

arc_clue.found: a letter addressed to Tamsin, posted fifteen years ago and never delivered, carries the tenth stud

volumes.method: hidden in plain sight (the missing item was never hidden, only disguised as something ordinary)

volumes.title: The Bookbinders' Odd Job
volumes.setting: a bookbinders' guild hall next to a private bank vault
volumes.clue_mechanic: schedule overlap (why was one person kept busy at exactly that hour)

arc_clue.found: the decoy job was copying a page of Odile's atlas; the copy holds the eleventh stud

volumes.method: the decoy errand (a well-paid odd job keeps one person away while the real plan runs)

volumes.title: The Lighthouse at the Edge of the Map
volumes.setting: a storm lighthouse and observatory on an island that is on no map

inspired_by.work: The Problem of Cell 13 (escape idea only)
inspired_by.author: Jacques Futrelle

volumes.clue_mechanic: impossible escape (only the objects in the room, used in the right order)
volumes.final_form: compass route built from all twelve studs

twists.shift: double shift seeded by the place name

arc_clue.found: the twelfth stud; the twelve letters spell HOLLOWAYMERE and the bearings lead to Odile, alive, keeping the atlas safe

volumes.method: the impossible escape (getting out of a locked tower with only what is in the room)

series_arc.model: Each volume is a complete case. Under it runs ONE long mystery about the detective herself; every volume ends by handing the reader one small, real piece of it. The pieces only make sense together, and the last volume cannot be solved without the pieces from the earlier ones.
series_arc.secret: Fifteen years ago Tamsin's mother, the mapmaker Odile Hale, walked out of the family map shop with an unfinished atlas and was never seen again. Tamsin keeps Odile's brass travelling compass: its lid holds eight empty sockets and its needle does not point north.
series_arc.question: Where did Odile Hale go, and why does her compass point somewhere that is on no map?
series_arc.collectible: a small engraved brass compass stud: one is hidden in each of the 12 cases, each carries one letter and one bearing
series_arc.mechanic: The last page of every volume is the Compass Page: the reader records the stud's letter and bearing. Volume 12's final puzzle needs all twelve: the letters spell a place name (HOLLOWAYMERE), the bearings draw the route.
series_arc.patron_link: The mysterious patron who sends the letter fragments is Odile's old partner; the courier appears in volume 8, the patron in volume 12.
rules: the arc clue is found by solving the volume's own final puzzle, never handed out for free
an arc clue never spoils that volume's culprit
each volume's last line is a hook that points at the next stud
volume 12 answers the question fully and fairly: every piece was shown in an earlier volume
no element is taken from any existing detective series: names, secret, objects and plot are original
